newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's Bonny crude oil loadings resume - Shell.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's Bonny crude oil loadings resume - Shell.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Wednesday it had resumed the loading of Bonny oil and a force majeure declared since Monday on the crude had now been lifted.
"We are now loading. A tanker is moored and loading," said a Shell spokesman in Lagos.
"There is going to be a slippage of a couple of days in the loading schedule, thats all," he added.
The resumption followed the end on Wednesday morning of a strike by staff Ocean Inchcape Limited (OIL), a contractor to Shell which handles the berthing and loading of oil tankers.
Shell declared force majeure on Bonny exports with effect from Monday when OIL staff began a strike demanding a pay-off because O.I.L had been sold to U.S.-based Tidewater Inc.
Shell said the force majeure was lifted on Wednesday afternoon. Bonny crude makes up roughly half of the 950,000 barrels per day of the crude oil produced by Shell in Nigeria.

Its oil production is also being threatened in the Warri area in the midwest where there has been tribal fighting over relocation of a local government area but the Shell spokesman said the situation there remained unchanged from the weekend when one flow station was shut down with loss of 2,000 bpd.
